id.description: The app in the API, assigned by the cloud and stable for the life of the app. Everything app-scoped takes this as its `:id`.

org_id.description: The organisation that owns this app. Every developer route is already scoped to the caller's org, so this confirms what a client is looking at rather than being a filter it applies.

name.description: The display name, shown in the console and available to the developer's own pages through the `app.name` mail-template variable. Free text, changed through `PATCH /api/apps/:id`.

identifier.description: The stable handle a client sends at login, lowercase and underscore-separated. **Globally unique, not per organisation** — `clientLoginRequest` carries no org context to disambiguate with, so a collision is refused with `identifier_taken`.

robot_ids.description: The robots this app may reach, each referenced individually. Tags never grant rights, and a robot absent from this list is invisible to the app whatever a role grants.

default_role_id.description: The role an app user gets when they are created or invited without an explicit one. `null` means this app has not chosen a default, the normal state of an app created before its roles were configured — and then a create or invite that omits `role_id` is a `validation_error` rather than a user with no role. An invitation resolves the role when it is issued, so changing this never re-aims an outstanding one. The role must belong to this app, which `PATCH /api/apps/:id` checks and the schema cannot.

created_at.description: When the app was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `GET /api/apps` orders by this field.
